TALES.name: The Bottle's Cargo
TALES.trouble: Someone corked a note and a promise into a bottle and set it adrift. The promise was never kept. The sea has had it a long time.
TALES.begin: Any drift bottle on the open sea. Sail alongside it and press the use key.

steps.say: Read the note in a drift bottle.
steps.did: You read the note. It names an islet.

steps.say: Dig up the cache the note points to. The Dreamvane's dowse finds it.
steps.did: A buried cache, dug. Someone's savings, sat in the sand.

steps.say: Make a singing stone's phrase answer on the Crucibelle.
steps.did: The stone answered. Something rose out of the sand.

steps.say: Photograph a herd at sea. The dock board says where one is today.
steps.did: A herd on a plate. The board pays for those.

steps.say: Sink a sea serpent, or any of the sea's beasts.
steps.did: The beast is down. The promise is kept, in its way.

TALES.name: The Ladle with No Bottom
TALES.trouble: A monk rises out of calm night water and asks sailors for a ladle. Whoever gives him one is drowned in the water it fills. He wants to be given something that cannot fill.
TALES.begin: Haul a crate up from any wreck, then read a stele on an islet.

steps.say: Haul a crate up from a wreck with the Sondelass worn.
steps.did: A crate, aboard. The wreck remembers who sank it.

steps.say: Read a stele on an islet.
steps.did: Three words on a stone, in a sentence. One of them is a ladle.

steps.say: Record 3 habits on plates. Creatures show them only under their own conditions.
steps.did: Three habits recorded. Habits are where the stories come from.

steps.say: Drink the umibozu's pour with the Lockheart's gulp until its hands let go.
steps.did: A ladle with no bottom, and the Lockheart drank it. The hands let go.
The monk goes under. Nobody drowned.

TALES.name: The Wind That Was Asked
TALES.who: An old sailor at the quay
TALES.trouble: An old sailor says the wind is a creature too, and creatures can be asked. Nobody believes her, because she never leaves the quay.
TALES.begin: Fit or make any ship's part at a quay, then sail until the sea is charted a little.

steps.say: Make a ship's part from its pieces at a quay (/shippart make).
steps.did: A part, made from pieces. The sailor nods once.

steps.say: Play the wind a song on the Crucibelle at the helm.
steps.did: The wind turned. An hour of it, for a price.

steps.say: Complete a square of the open sea: everything in it found, taken and salvaged.
steps.did: A square, finished. The sailor's chart has one more tick.

steps.say: Tow a stunned beast home alive to a quay.
steps.did: A creature, asked and not killed. That is the point the old sailor was making.
